description: Number of agents in the synthetic city.
notes: Age distribution of Salt Lake County, UT (2025 Census estimates, via multigroup.vaccine), rescaled to n, about a tenth of the county estimate (1,220,916).

description: Number of infections at the start of each simulation (in the latent state).
Basic reproduction number targeted when calibrating the contact matrix.
notes: Below the 12-18 range of Guerra et al. 2017 (Lancet Infect Dis 17(12):e420-e428); the measles package uses 15. Not a model argument: it enters through the calibrated contact matrix.

description: MMR coverage of adults aged 45-69; ages 25-44 take the mean of this and the high-school coverage.
notes: Under 1s are unvaccinated, ages 1-4 take the elementary-school coverage and ages 5-24 out of school the high-school coverage (community_coverage() in model.R).

description: Agents of this age and older count as vaccinated.
citation: Presumptive evidence of immunity: birth before 1957 (CDC)
notes: The 70-74 band approximates birth before 1957 in 2026.

description: Efficacy of two doses of MMR vaccine.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026) ("~97%")
notes: Same as the measles package.

description: Probability of transmission per contact between an infectious and a susceptible agent.
citation: Assumption: highly transmissible; Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): "90% of susceptible contacts will develop disease"
notes: Calibrated to R0 with contacts fixed from the setting matrices: next-generation starting value (transmission_for_r0() in model.R), refined by simulation.

description: Average days from exposure to the start of the prodromal (infectious) period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): exposure to prodrome averages 8-12 days
notes: The measles package uses 12.

description: Standard deviation of lognormal stage duration.
notes: Applied to exposure-to-prodrome as an approximation; Lessler estimates exposure-to-first-symptoms.

description: Average days of the infectious prodromal period, before rash onset.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): prodrome lasts 2-4 days (range 2-8); contagious 4 days before rash onset
notes: Same as the measles package.

description: Standard deviation of lognormal stage duration.
notes: Estimated from 188 historical cases.

description: Average days of the infectious part of the rash period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): contagious to 4 days after rash onset
notes: The measles package uses 3 (infectivity is minimal after day 2 of rash).

description: Standard deviation of lognormal stage duration.
notes: No direct fit for infectious rash duration.

description: Probability that an infection is hospitalized during the rash period.
citation: Derived: share of reported cases hospitalized times the reporting fraction
notes: 8% of reported cases in Utah (Jones et al. 2026, NEJM Evid 5(8)) times 25% reported gives 2% of infections; 18.5% in West Texas (Wang et al. 2026, MMWR 75:252-257) would give 4.6%. Converted to a daily probability using the rash-duration distribution. Hospitalized cases count as reported.

description: Average days in hospital.
notes: Observed stays are shorter: a mean of 2.1 nights in Utah (Jones et al. 2026).

description: Number of simulated days.
Day of peak shedding, counted from prodrome onset (4 = rash onset).
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026, Emerg Infect Dis 32(10): shedding during the prodrome and around rash onset

description: Days before prodrome onset when shedding into wastewater starts; must not exceed ww_lab_delay.
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026, Emerg Infect Dis 32(10): RNA shed during the prodrome, before rash onset
notes: No data found on urine or fecal shedding before the prodrome; contagiousness starts about 4 days before rash (prodrome onset).

description: Last day of shedding, counted from prodrome onset (about 14 days after rash onset).
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: urine RNA up to 14 days; CDC: RT-PCR positive up to 10+ days after rash

description: Ratio between the peak and the ends of the shedding profile (log10 scale).
notes: Only sets the shape; the profile is normalized to sum to one.

description: Mean of the log10 total genome copies shed per infection (log-normal).
citation: STOTEN 2024: about 10^8.7 copies per infection per day over about 2 weeks; Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: median 1.4 x 10^11 copies per person per day

description: Standard deviation of the log10 total genome copies shed per infection.
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: shedding spans four orders of magnitude

description: Wastewater volume per person per day.
Standard deviation of the log-normal measurement error.
Measurements below the LOD are recorded as non-detects (3 log10 copies/L).
Days of the week (t %% 7) when wastewater is sampled: twice a week.
citation: Utah practice: measles samples twice a week (Deseret News, March 21, 2026)
notes: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026 sampled three times a week in Ontario. Scenarios override this in scenarios.yml.

description: Days from sample collection until the result is available to act on.
citation: Provo, UT (2025): 4 days from collection to DHHS notification by WastewaterSCAN; Utah pilot (2020), transport within 24 h and a 48-h lab turnaround; NWSS, a median of 2 days (IQR 1-4) from collection to testing; New Mexico (2025), results within 10 days
notes: The wastewater scenario uses 4 days (Provo) and wastewater-fast 2 days (Utah pilot, NWSS median); see scenarios.yml.

description: Days from rash onset until a detected case is reported.
notes: The measles package assumes 2 days from rash onset to detection.

description: Share of infections that are reported, through detection during rash or hospitalization.
citation: Hidden Burden of a Measles Outbreak Revealed by Genomic and Transmission Models (EpiForeSITE): about 25% of cases reported in southwest Utah
notes: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026 estimated 5-10x under-reporting in Ontario.

description: Daily probability that a case with rash is detected; detected cases are isolated and reported.
notes: Solved so that detections plus hospitalizations report reporting_fraction of cases; about 0.06 with the defaults.

description: Share of infections reported while a public health alert is active (e.g., health alerts to clinicians, more testing and exposure notification).
notes: Sets alert_detection_rate. The alert follows any reported case and, in the wastewater response, any positive wastewater result.

description: Daily detection probability while a public health alert is active.
Concentration at or above which a sample is positive.
notes: Fixed at the limit of detection, so any detection is positive.

description: Days a school exclusion or public health alert lasts after the last reported case or positive result.
citation: Two incubation periods, the usual criterion to declare a measles outbreak over
notes: Each new report or positive result restarts the period.

description: Probability that a sample is positive without a true signal (e.g., vaccine-strain shedding or lab error).
notes: About 0.5 false positives a year at two samples a week.

description: Target number of students per simulated school.
notes: Each simulated school takes the MMR coverage of a source school of its level.
